HR & Benefits Policy
[Company Name] Corporate Guidelines
Effective Date: [Date]
Version: 1.1
Doc Ref: HR-POL-002
This document outlines the core human resources policies at [Company Name]. These guidelines are
designed to promote a healthy work-life balance, ensure operational continuity, and provide
comprehensive support to our employees.

1. Employee Leave Policy (Annual & Sick Leave)
We believe that regular time away from work is essential for employee well-being and sustained
productivity. All full-time employees are entitled to comprehensive paid time off (PTO) as structured below.
1.1 LEAVE CATEGORIES AND ACCRUAL
Earned Leave (EL)
Employees are allotted 20 days of Earned Leave annually. This leave is accrued monthly at a rate of 1.66

. This leave is accrued monthly at a rate of 1.66
days per month. Up to 10 days of unused Earned Leave can be rolled over to the next calendar year; any
excess leave will expire at the end of the year.
Sick Leave (SL)
A total of 10 days of Sick Leave is provided each year. This is credited in full on January 1st. Sick leave
does not carry forward and will lapse at year-end if unused.
Casual Leave (CL)

ll lapse at year-end if unused.
Casual Leave (CL)
Employees receive 5 days of Casual Leave annually, credited in full on January 1st. Similar to sick leave,
casual leave does not carry forward and lapses at the end of the calendar year.

1.2 BUSINESS RULES FOR GENERAL LEAVE
Approval Process: All Earned Leave and Casual Leave requests must be submitted via the HR
Portal at least two weeks in advance. Approval is subject to managerial discretion and team
coverage requirements.
Unplanned Leave: In the event of sudden illness, employees must notify their immediate
supervisor within two hours of their scheduled start time.
Medical Certification: Sick leave exceeding three (3) consecutive days requires a certified medical

(3) consecutive days requires a certified medical
certificate from a registered practitioner upon returning to work.
Probationary Employees: Employees on probation are only eligible to utilize accrued Sick Leave.
Earned Leave can be utilized post-confirmation.

Note on Public Holidays: The company observes [Number] mandatory public holidays and [Number]
optional floating holidays annually. The official calendar is published by HR in December of the preceding
year.

2. Maternity & Paternity Leave Policy
We are committed to supporting our employees as they grow their families. Our family leave policies are
designed to provide financial security, job protection, and vital time for bonding with new additions to the
family.
2.1 MATERNITY LEAVE
Maternity leave is provided to support female employees during the final stages of pregnancy and the
critical initial months of motherhood.
Entitlement and Eligibility

months of motherhood.
Entitlement and Eligibility
Female employees are entitled to 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave for their first two children. For
subsequent children, the entitlement is 12 weeks of paid leave. To be eligible, the employee must have
worked for the company for a minimum of 80 days in the 12 months immediately preceding the expected
date of delivery.
Utilization Guidelines

expected
date of delivery.
Utilization Guidelines
Employees may choose to begin their maternity leave up to 8 weeks prior to the expected delivery date,
with the remaining 18 weeks taken post-delivery. Medical certification of the expected delivery date must
be provided to HR at least 30 days before the commencement of the leave.

Adoption & Surrogacy
A maximum of 12 weeks of paid leave is granted to commissioning mothers and adopting mothers. This
applies when legally adopting a child below the age of three months, starting from the date the child is
handed over.

2.2 PATERNITY LEAVE
Paternity leave is provided to encourage shared parenting responsibilities and support partners during the
immediate post-natal period.
Entitlement
Male employees are eligible for 4 weeks of fully paid paternity leave upon the birth or legal adoption of a
child.
Utilization Guidelines
Paternity leave must be utilized within 6 months of the child's birth or adoption date. It can be taken in a

ld's birth or adoption date. It can be taken in a
single continuous block of 4 weeks, or split into two separate parts of 2 weeks each, subject to manager
approval.

3. Remote Work & Telecommuting Policy
[Company Name] embraces a flexible, modern working environment. This policy defines the operational
guidelines for remote work to ensure employees remain connected, highly productive, and secure
regardless of their physical location.
3.1 HYBRID WORKING MODEL
Unless specifically contracted as a fully remote employee, all staff operate on a structured hybrid model
designed to balance in-person collaboration with focused remote work:

in-person collaboration with focused remote work:
Office Days: Employees are required to work from their designated primary office location for a
minimum of 3 days per week.
Remote Days: Up to 2 days per week may be worked remotely from an appropriate home
environment. Remote days must be scheduled in coordination with the team manager to ensure
adequate in-office coverage for client meetings and collaborative sessions.

e for client meetings and collaborative sessions.
Core Collaborative Hours: Regardless of physical location, employees must be online,
responsive, and available for team meetings during the company's core collaborative hours of 10:00
AM to 4:00 PM [Timezone].

3.2 EQUIPMENT, ALLOWANCE, AND WORKSPACE
To ensure remote days are as productive as office days, the company provides support for home office
environments.
Company Assets: The company will provide a standard-issue laptop and all necessary licensed
software.
Home Office Setup: A one-time allowance of [Amount] is available for employees to enhance their
home office setup (e.g., purchasing an ergonomic chair, external monitor, or dedicated desk). This is

ir, external monitor, or dedicated desk). This is
claimable via the HR portal with valid receipts.

3.3 SECURITY AND DATA PRIVACY
Protecting company and client data is paramount, particularly when operating outside the corporate
firewall.
Network Security: Employees must use the company-provided VPN at all times when accessing
internal networks, codebases, or customer databases. Working from public, unsecured Wi-Fi
networks (e.g., coffee shops, airports) without the VPN active is strictly prohibited.
Data Privacy: Physical documents containing confidential company or client data must not be

g confidential company or client data must not be
printed or stored at a home office. Screen privacy must be actively maintained if an employee is
working temporarily in a shared or semi-public space.

4. Medical Insurance Policy
To safeguard the physical health and financial well-being of our workforce, the company provides
comprehensive Group Medical Health Insurance through our partnered provider, [Insurance Provider
Name].
4.1 COVERAGE SUMMARY
Family Floater Sum Insured
The policy provides a generous primary coverage amount of [Amount, e.g., $100,000 / ₹5,00,000] per
family per annum. This sum floats across all enrolled family members.
Covered Dependents

s all enrolled family members.
Covered Dependents
Coverage extends automatically to the employee, their legally married spouse, and up to two (2)
dependent children under the age of 25 years.
Pre-Existing Diseases
All pre-existing medical conditions and diseases are fully covered from Day 1 of the policy. There are
absolutely no waiting periods applied to new employees or their newly added dependents.
Maternity Benefit

r their newly added dependents.
Maternity Benefit
Maternity-related hospital expenses are covered up to [Amount] for normal deliveries and up to [Amount]
for medically required C-section procedures.
Room Rent Limit
There is no financial capping or sub-limit on room rent. Employees and their dependents are eligible for a
single private A/C room during hospitalization, subject to availability at the medical facility.

4.2 ENROLLMENT AND CLAIM PROCESS
Enrollment: New employees must complete the insurance enrollment form via the HR portal within
7 days of their joining date. Dependent additions (such as marriage or the birth of a child) must be
updated in the system within 30 days of the qualifying life event.
Cashless Claims: Treatment at network hospitals can be availed directly by presenting the
corporate e-Health card at the insurance desk. Approvals and billing are processed directly between

rovals and billing are processed directly between
the hospital and the Third Party Administrator (TPA).
Reimbursement Claims: For treatments at non-network hospitals, employees must settle the bill
upfront. Original bills, discharge summaries, and standard claim forms must be submitted physically
to the HR desk within 15 days of discharge for prompt reimbursement.

EMPLOYEE ACKNOWLEDGMENT
By signing below, I acknowledge that I have received, read, and understood the policies outlined
in this document. I agree to comply with the rules and guidelines stated herein. I understand that
the company reserves the right to amend these policies with due notice.
